findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: Food handler stated the facility has been using the dish machine to sanitize dishes and other food contact surfaces. The facility was instructed to utilize the triple sink to wash and sanitize food contact surfaces until the heat sanitizing dish machine was serviced, AND the facility had a way to verify proper sanitizing temperatures are being reached until the dish machine. CORRECTED- Education occurred with the PIC, who was reminded that the dish machine is not to be used until proper heat sanitizing temperatures are reached, and the facility is able to verify proper sanitizing temperatures. The heat sanitizing dish machine took over 1 hour to heat up during the inspection. Ensure employees utilize the triple sink for sanitation OR wait until the dish machine reaches a minimum wash temperature of 160, and minimum rinse temperature of 180 to use the dish machine for heat sanitation.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(L) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (L) EMPLOYEES are properly SANITIZING cleaned multiuse EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS before they are reused, through routine monitoring of solution temperature and exposure time for hot water SANITIZING, and chemical concentration, pH, temperature, and exposure time for chemical SANITIZING. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The designated person in charge (PIC) was unable to locate heat test strips during today’s re-inspection. They have ordered strips, and they have an invoice stating they have been delivered, but the facility could not produce the heat temperature test strips. Facilities that use heat for sanitation need heat test strips or a surface temperature dish plate to verify that the machine is reaching proper sanitizing temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed heat dish plate for the facility’s heat sanitizing dish machine to reach a surface temperature of 150F, after 3 wash and rinse cycles. Person in charge (PIC) placed a work order for the dish machine. Facility is instructed to utilize the 3 compartment sink for sanitizing food contact services until the dish machine is serviced. Dish machines that use heat for sanitation must reach a minimum temperature of 165F.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no device to test the temperature of the heat sanitizing dish machine. PIC and other staff members were unable to locate the strips during this inspection. Obtain test strips to ensure that heat sanitizing dish machine is reaching minimum required sanitation temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 A heat sanitizing dish machine is used for large pots and pans. Facility does not currently have an irreversible registering temperature indicator for checking the surface temperature at the dishes during a ware washing cycle. Options for dish machine temperature test strips and maximum registering thermometers were discussed. Dish machine temperature test strips were ordered during inspection. 
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.
